name: Jennifer (Burgess) Daljeet
headline: Director of Clinical Practice at St. Peter's Residence at Chedoke
about:
With more than 23 years of experience in the care of older adults, nursing education, and primary care, I am committed to delivering high-quality, evidence-based care in long-term care settings.

My areas of expertise include chronic disease management, acute episodic care, palliative care, nursing education, infection prevention and control, and advanced wound assessment and management.

I hold a Master of Science in Nursing and a Primary Health Care Nurse Practitioner certificate from McMaster University, as well as Gerontological Nursing Certification from the Canadian Nurses Association. I have also contributed to research and publications focused on fracture prevention and management, and the COVID-19 response in long-term care.
… more

experiences.description: Provided leadership for the Medical Services program, working alongside the Medical Director, and providing direct primary care for residents.  I am also responsible for the development and leadership of the IPAC program and contribute to clinical skills development for the nursing team. I have taken initiative for additional clinical development in the home including antimicrobial stewardship,  fracture prevention, and reduction of polypharmacy.

experiences.companyName: HNHB Nurse Led Outreach Team (Shalom Village)
experiences.description: In a collaborative clinical model, I provided primary care to LTC residents in the Hamilton and Burlington area LTC Homes in order to avert transfers to the Emergency Department, partnered with the ED to avoid hospital admissions, facilitated timely discharges from hospital, and supported preventative care.  I had ongoing collaboration with system partners on initiatives including the development of LTC-CARES Hamilton and contribution to the community advanced paramedicine program.
In this role I provided capacity building, education, collaboration, consulting and partnership within 87 LTC homes and community partners in the HNHB LHIN.

In this role I was responsible for frontline nursing care of 33 residents in long-term care, coordination of care, care planning, and RAI-MDS.  I was also responsible for the development of both wound and palliative care programs.
At the beginning of my nursing career, I was Charge Nurse for 192 LTC residents and staff and later took on a Clinical Lead role as a support to the nursing team.
